end.summary:
Pari practised naming common non-metals and identifying their states.
They correctly identified oxygen and nitrogen as gases, carbon and iodine as solids.
They connected nitrogen with plant growth, urea, and fertilisers.
They connected graphite with pencils, oxygen with respiration and burning, and chlorine with gas particles.
Teach-back was not passed; no recorded misconception was corrected later.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the states of common non-metals and their everyday uses with Pari. Pari used examples such as pencils, plants, breathing, and a gas stove to explain ideas, and correctly connected graphite with carbon and nitrogen with plant growth and fertilisers. One question was left unanswered, and no mix-up was recorded as corrected later. At home, ask Pari to sort oxygen, nitrogen, carbon, sulphur, chlorine, iodine, hydrogen, helium, and phosphorus into solid, liquid, and gas, then match each with one use.
